title: Global Ranking Check
description: Predict how a numeric rank maps to a tier, and what drives rank in the first place.

questions.prompt: What primarily drives a HackerRank global rank number?
questions.explanation: Rank is computed mostly from rated contest performance, not from untimed practice activity.

questions.prompt: Which rank is the stronger signal: #57 or #15234?

options.text: #15234, because higher numbers mean more points
#57, because a smaller rank number is better
Neither — rank has no meaningful ordering

questions.explanation: Rank works opposite to score: a lower number means a stronger relative standing.

questions.prompt: Using top-100 (<=100), top-1000 (<=1000), open (else), what tier is rank exactly 1000?
questions.explanation: 1000 is inclusive in the top-1000 band since it satisfies rank <= 1000 while being greater than 100.

questions.prompt: Why might a profile with lots of practice challenges solved have no meaningful contest rank?

options.text: Practice challenges don't feed into the rated contest rank
Rank is disabled for profiles with a high score
Practice and rank use the same formula, so this can't happen

questions.explanation: Rank is tied to rated contest participation, so untimed practice alone doesn't necessarily produce a meaningful rank.

questions.prompt: Most active users fall into the `open` tier. What does that imply?

options.text: Landing in `open` is expected and not, by itself, a weak signal

questions.explanation: The top tiers are narrow bands by design — most users, including strong ones, fall into the broad open range.
